cases.name: b1c.dual.levi_civita_normalisation
cases.notes: the contravariant sign is forced by the (-,+,+,+) signature, not chosen; the curved lab would catch a hard-coded Minkowski symbol
cases.reference: eps_{0123} = +sqrt(-det g) and eps^{0123} = -1/sqrt(-det g), both totally antisymmetric, for Minkowski AND a curved non-diagonal lab

cases.name: b1c.dual.contraction_identity
cases.notes: the minus sign here is the source of **F = -F; checking it directly means the double-dual result is explained, not just observed
cases.reference: eps_{abcd} eps^{cdef} = -2(delta_a^e delta_b^f - delta_a^f delta_b^e)

cases.name: b1c.dual.two_form_double_dual_is_minus_identity
cases.notes: CONFIRMED SIGN: minus. In Riemannian signature it would be +F, so this pins the signature-dependent branch of the convention
cases.reference: **F = -F for an arbitrary two-form, in four-dimensional Lorentzian signature

cases.name: b1c.dual.left_dual_squared_is_minus_identity
cases.parameters: random Z with Z's antisymmetries; Minkowski and curved lab

cases.name: b1c.dual.right_dual_squared_is_minus_identity
cases.parameters: random Z with Z's antisymmetries; Minkowski and curved lab

cases.name: b1c.dual.left_right_commute
cases.reference: *(Z*) = (*Z)*, since the two duals contract disjoint index pairs

cases.name: b1c.dual.double_dual_squared_is_identity
cases.reference: (*Z*) applied twice returns +Z: (-1) from each index pair

cases.name: b1c.dual.vacuum_analytic
cases.notes: an independent closed form, not a self-consistency identity
cases.reference: the left dual of the vacuum Z equals (1/2) eps^{abcd}

cases.name: b1c.dual.transforms_tensorially
cases.notes: det L != 1 deliberately: a dual built from a bare permutation symbol rather than the Levi-Civita TENSOR would fail exactly here
cases.reference: *(L.Z) computed in the new coordinates equals L.(*Z) computed in the old ones

cases.name: b1c.covariant_minkowski_is_vacuum
cases.notes: pins the 1/2 in the definition of Z and the absence of a second 1/2 in the constitutive relation
cases.reference: H^{ab} = Z^{abcd} F_{cd} reproduces H = F exactly for Minkowski, on a general antisymmetric F

cases.name: b1c.covariant_conformal_invariance
cases.notes: density factor Omega^4 against Omega^-4 from the two inverse metrics
cases.reference: Z^{abcd} is unchanged under g_eff -> Omega^2 g_eff

cases.name: b1c.covariant_transforms_tensorially
cases.notes: a coordinate artefact must not be mistaken for invariant non-realizability, so the tensorial character is checked directly
cases.parameters: rotation by 0.6 rad plus a z rescale
cases.reference: Z'^{abcd} = L^a_p L^b_q L^c_r L^d_s Z^{pqrs} under a linear change of coordinates applied to both g_eff and g_lab

cases.name: b1c.warp_epsilon_closed_form
cases.notes: derived: eps^{ij} = -g^{00}(gamma^-1)^{ij}, and the Alcubierre spatial block is delta_ij with det g = -1, so g^{00} = -1. This is why the withdrawn cond(eps) divergence test could never fire
cases.reference: eps^{ab} = h^{ab} exactly for the Alcubierre analogue with g_lab = eta and the laboratory rest observer, at every v_s

cases.name: b1c.warp_mu_inverse_closed_form
cases.notes: the transverse eigenvalue is exactly -g_00 and therefore passes through ZERO on the ergosurface: mu itself diverges there. That is the quantity which actually blows up for this observer

cases.name: b1c.warp_zeta_closed_form
cases.notes: an exact signed closed form for the warp medium's magnetoelectric block. Replaces the withdrawn min(error_to_xi, error_to_zeta) comparison, which asserted no sign at all
cases.reference: zeta^{23} = -g_01 = v f, zeta^{32} = +g_01, all other components zero

cases.name: b1c.warp_blocks_are_reciprocal
cases.reference: zeta_adjoint = zeta^T for the warp analogue, as required by the pair symmetry Z^{abcd} = Z^{cdab}

cases.name: b1c.warp_magnetoelectric_handedness
cases.notes: one direction is asserted; a +y result fails. Same handedness as the moving isotropic medium of B1C-S456, which is checked against Minkowski's moving-medium relations
cases.reference: for the warp analogue with the bubble moving along +x, B = +B0 z-hat and E = 0, the induced displacement points along -y

cases.name: b1c.warp_magnetoelectric_magnitude
cases.reference: D_y = g_01 = -v f B0 exactly

cases.name: b1c.plebanski_epsilon_closed_form
cases.notes: its own closed form, in its own g_00 normalisation. Compare with b1c.warp_epsilon_closed_form, which is the IDENTITY: the two differ by exactly 1/(1-v^2f^2) and cannot both be eps for one observer
cases.reference: the Plebanski eps is diag(1, 1/(1-v^2f^2), 1/(1-v^2f^2)) for the Alcubierre metric

cases.name: b1c.plebanski_differs_by_observer_normalisation
cases.notes: THE WITHDRAWN EQUALITY. The old case asserted these were equal to 1e-12 and failed by 4.1667e-2 = 1/24 = 1/(1-0.04) - 1 at v_s=0.2, f=1. Plebanski's 3+1 tensors are normalised by g_00 of g_eff; the (A7) blocks are normalised by g_lab. They are different observers and must not be compared for equality
cases.reference: the covariant eps for the laboratory observer and the Plebanski eps differ, by exactly the ratio of the two observers' normalisations

cases.name: b1c.plebanski_mu_inverse_coincides
cases.notes: this coincidence is real and is retained as a cross-check between two independent routes, but it is NOT evidence that the two observers agree -- eps demonstrably does not. It is special to a metric whose spatial block is delta_ij
cases.reference: [mu^-1] from the (A7) laboratory decomposition equals the 3x3 inverse of the Plebanski mu, componentwise

cases.expected_description: smallest block difference above 1e-3 over all such points
cases.name: b1c.observer_change_blocks_differ_over_profile
cases.notes: without this the agreement below would say nothing about observer independence
cases.reference: at every profile point where the medium is not vacuum, two admissible laboratory observers see different blocks

cases.name: b1c.observer_change_reconstruction_over_profile
cases.notes: this is what replaces the withdrawn comparison of one observer's blocks against another's. Observer-dependent quantities are not asserted equal; the tensor they rebuild is
cases.parameters: v_s in {0.2,0.4,2}, six positions each, V = lab rest and U = boosted beta_y = 0.5
cases.reference: Zhat[V] = Z, Zhat[U] = Z and Zhat[V] = Zhat[U] across the warp profile: the blocks are observer dependent, the tensor is not

cases.computed_description: 241 points with g_00 >= 0; covariant Z valid at 241; g_eff Lorentzian at 241; coordinate-time observer of g_eff inadmissible at 241
cases.expected_description: covariant valid everywhere, observer invalid everywhere
cases.name: b1c.ergoregion_covariant_valid_observer_fails
cases.notes: THIS IS THE CORRECTION. B1 reported 'no equivalent medium exists' here. What actually fails is one observer's decomposition. The surface is an ERGOSURFACE, not an invariant realizability wall
cases.reference: inside v_s f > 1 the effective metric stays Lorentzian and Z^{abcd} stays valid at EVERY point, while the coordinate-time observer of g_eff is inadmissible at every point

cases.name: b1c.alcubierre_lorentzian_at_all_velocities
cases.notes: the (t,x) block has determinant -1 identically, so its two eigenvalues always have opposite signs however large v_s f is. This is why no invariant obstruction exists at v_s f = 1
cases.reference: the Alcubierre metric has signature (-,+,+,+) and det g = -1 at every point for v_s up to 10

cases.computed_description: 201 ergoregion points: Eulerian observer of g_eff admissible at 201, laboratory observer at 201, laboratory (A7) blocks finite at 201
cases.expected_description: both alternatives admissible and the blocks finite throughout
cases.name: b1c.alternative_observers_in_ergoregion
cases.notes: demonstrates directly that the failure is observer-dependent: changing observer removes it
cases.reference: inside the ergoregion the Eulerian observer of g_eff and the laboratory observer both remain admissible where the g_eff coordinate-time observer does not, and the laboratory blocks stay finite

cases.expected_description: 3 valid decompositions, all differing from the rest-frame one
cases.name: b1c.boosted_observer_blocks_differ
cases.notes: eps, mu^-1 and zeta are observer-dependent by construction. If they had come out identical, the decomposition would be ignoring V. Supersedes b1c.boosted_observer_decomposition, which measured the same property through the quarantined tetrad path
cases.reference: a boosted inertial laboratory observer gives a valid but DIFFERENT (A7) decomposition of the same Z

cases.name: b1c.ergosurface.epsilon_is_the_projector
cases.notes: THE WITHDRAWN ASSERTION, restated as what is actually true. The old case demanded cond(eps) > 10 x its far value and measured 1 versus 1. A uniformly scaling tensor keeps condition number 1; eps here does not even scale
cases.parameters: v_s = 2, x from 2 to 5 through the ergosurface
cases.reference: eps^{ab} = h^{ab} at every point of the sweep, so its condition number is identically 1 and cannot diverge

cases.computed_description: cond(eps) = 1 nearest the ergosurface (|g_00| = 2.4577e-05) versus 1 at x = 5
cases.name: b1c.ergosurface.epsilon_conditioning_does_not_diverge
cases.notes: this case exists to keep the withdrawal visible in the gate output rather than only in the audit document
cases.reference: cond(eps) is 1 both at the ergosurface and far from it, recorded so the withdrawn expectation is not silently dropped

cases.name: b1c.ergosurface.mu_inverse_min_eigenvalue_closed_form
cases.notes: the spectrum is {1, -g_00, -g_00}, so the transverse pair reaches zero precisely on the ergosurface and mu = (mu^-1)^-1 diverges there. It is min(1, |g_00|) and NOT |g_00|: deep inside the ergoregion |g_00| = |1 - v^2f^2| exceeds 1 -- 2.97 at x = 2 for v_s = 2 -- and the unit longitudinal eigenvalue is then the smaller one. This is the quantity actually predicted to diverge for this observer
cases.parameters: v_s = 2, x from 2 to 5 through the ergosurface
cases.reference: the smallest eigenvalue magnitude of [mu^-1] equals min(1, |g_00|) exactly along the sweep

cases.expected_description: mu^-1 degenerate near the surface, unit far away
cases.name: b1c.ergosurface.permeability_diverges
cases.notes: asserted for a quantity predicted to diverge, under the same observer and the same conventions as the decomposition. Replaces b1c.eigenvalue_conditioning_diverges_at_ergosurface
cases.reference: the permeability diverges at the ergosurface: min|eig mu^-1| falls below 1e-4, cond(mu^-1) exceeds 1e3 and |det mu^-1| falls below 1e-8, while all three are of order 1 far away

cases.computed_description: max|Z| = 0.500006 nearest the ergosurface versus 0.5 at x = 5, difference 6.14421e-06; range over the whole sweep [0.5, 1.42875]; max|zeta| = 1.00001 versus 0.000670709
cases.expected_description: max|Z| in (0.1, 2) throughout, and near == far to 1e-4; max|zeta| finite
cases.name: b1c.ergosurface.covariant_tensor_stays_bounded
cases.notes: the two halves of the correction in one measurement: the covariant tensor does not notice the ergosurface, one observer's material parameters do. max|Z| is bounded but NOT constant over the sweep -- it rises to about 1.49 deep inside the ergoregion, where g_eff^{11} = 1 - v^2f^2 reaches -2.98 -- so boundedness is what is asserted, not constancy
cases.reference: max|Z^{abcd}| is bounded over the whole sweep and is unchanged to 1e-4 across the ergosurface itself, and the magnetoelectric norm stays finite, while the permeability diverges
